key_insight: The paper shows how to turn standard neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that work directly with continuous function spaces. This makes learned scientific models more reliable when applied across different grid resolutions and simulation settings.
problem_solved: Many neural architectures are tied to the resolution of the training data, which makes them brittle when scientific simulations are represented on different meshes, grids, or discretizations. The paper addresses how to extend these models so they can learn operators over continuous data rather than fixed-size arrays.
method: Reformulate popular neural network architectures as neural operators that map between functions instead of finite-dimensional vectors.
Design principled extensions that preserve the original network’s useful inductive biases while making them agnostic to discretization.
Train on continuous scientific data so the model can generalize across resolutions and sampling schemes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical path to building models that transfer better across simulation resolutions and scientific domains. It is especially useful for physics-informed learning, surrogate modeling, and numerical science workflows where discretization mismatch is a major limitation.

paper_title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
paper_authors: Julius Berner, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Jean Kossaifi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev
